title: Quickstarts: add marketplace buyer activation path (org linking + validation)
author: Elliot Price
description:
Context: We’re seeing repeated friction for AWS/GCP Marketplace buyers after purchase: they don’t know which Redwood org to link, which env vars are required, and how to verify entitlements are active before trying the API. This PR adds an explicit “Marketplace buyer” path to the quickstarts with (1) a minimal set of marketplace-specific env vars, (2) an org-linking step that matches the Console wizard, and (3) a validation command that fails fast with actionable output.

What’s included:
- New docs section: Marketplace buyer path (AWS/GCP) added to the top-level onboarding README, with a short decision tree (“Direct signup” vs “Marketplace purchase”).
- New env var set:
  - REDWOOD_ORG_ID (required for marketplace purchases; used to disambiguate org linking)
  - REDWOOD_MARKETPLACE_PROVIDER (aws|gcp)
  - REDWOOD_MARKETPLACE_ACCOUNT_ID (AWS payer account / GCP billing account reference, depending on provider)
  - REDWOOD_REGION (optional; used to catch the common ‘region mismatch’ issue early)
- Org linking step:
  - Adds a dedicated step that points the user to the Console “Link marketplace purchase” page, and explains where to find Org ID.
  - Adds guidance for the two common edge cases: multiple cloud accounts and linking to the wrong Redwood org.
- Validation command:
  - Adds ./scripts/validate-marketplace-activation (bash + node wrapper) that calls the Redwood API endpoint used by the Console to check entitlement state.
  - Output is designed to be copy/pasteable into support tickets (includes request id, org id, provider, entitlement status, and recommended next step).

Not included / follow-ups:
- No changes to backend entitlement mapping; this PR is only quickstart UX and a lightweight validation script.
- The validation endpoint used here is already public for authenticated users, but error strings were chosen to align with ongoing Console copy work (DES-213).

How to test:
1) From a machine with node >=18:
   - cp .env.example .env
   - Fill in REDWOOD_API_KEY and marketplace vars (set provider to aws or gcp)
2) Run: ./scripts/validate-marketplace-activation
   - Expected: If entitlements are active, you see “ACTIVE” plus linked SKU(s).
   - If not active, you see “PENDING” with a suggested wait time and link to troubleshooting.
3) Proceed with existing chat/embeddings quickstarts using the same .env; no other changes required.

Why this helps:
- Reduces time-to-first-call for enterprise buyers who must procure through marketplace.
- Makes entitlement delays explicit and easier to diagnose (SUP-18420) and reduces accidental wrong-org linking (SUP-18433).

Screenshots: N/A (documentation + scripts only).

review_conversation:
Markus Klein (SE) 2025-02-04: The validation output should tell the user exactly what to do if it’s pending (wait vs contact support) and what info to include. Also, can we avoid saying ‘your purchase failed’ when it’s just propagation delay?

Elliot Price 2025-02-04: Good call. Updated copy to use PENDING + estimated propagation window, and added a ‘Support bundle’ block (org id, provider, account id, request id).

Chloe Martin 2025-02-05: The org linking step should match the Console naming. Console uses “Link marketplace purchase”, not “Connect billing”. Also please avoid instructing users to paste billing IDs into chat/support unless required.

Elliot Price 2025-02-05: Updated wording to “Link marketplace purchase”. Adjusted troubleshooting to only request provider + last 4 of account id by default, with full id optional when escalating.

Leila Farouk 2025-02-06: Ran through flow with dummy env values. Script exits 1 on missing vars (good). One request: make error messages deterministic so we can assert in CI later.

Elliot Price 2025-02-06: Implemented stable exit codes + consistent error prefixes (E_MKT_*). Added a small unit test for argument validation.

Markus Klein 2025-02-07: Approving. This matches the common buyer questions from recent calls and should reduce first-week support tickets.

Chloe Martin 2025-02-07: LGTM.

Leila Farouk 2025-02-07: Approved after rerun; CI green.
release_notes: Quickstarts now include a Marketplace buyer activation path with org-linking instructions and a validation script to confirm entitlement activation before running examples.
